newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF -DSM venture has 20 pct market.
newsitem.headline: BASF -DSM venture has 20 pct market.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG said on Monday its joint venture with Dutch group DSM NV would have a 20 percent share an otherwise highly fragmented European market for unsaturated polyester resins.

A spokesman for the German group said the two companies were looking to get economies of scale from being the largest European producer of the material, which is used in a range of automotive to construction applications.
"But this is more of an offensive than defensive step" the spokesman said. He said the move was not motivated by any perception of overcapacity in the sector.

BASF and DSM confirmed on Monday that they had agreed to merge their unsaturated polyester resin businesses to form a operation with some 450 million marks ($295.4 million) of annual sales. Plans for the move had been announced earlier this year in April.
BASF's spokesman said the venture, which will be 60 percent-owned by DSM, would be looking to develop new polyester resin-based products, particularly in the automotive sector.
"When we first announced plans for the merger, we had a very good response from clients who wanted to see a substantial, solid European supplier," he added.
Around two million tonnes of the material are produced annually worldwide, with the European market accounting for around a quarter of the total.
The spokesman said that BASF did not expect any further collobaration between the two.
